blog_posts.title: How to replace a harsh industrial cleaner without betting the facility
blog_posts.body:
## Why chemical replacements fail

A promising cleaner can fail for a boring reason: it was tested on the wrong soil, at the wrong dose, with no shared finish line. A fair trial removes that ambiguity before a facility changes its SOP.

The goal is not to make VertKleen look good. The goal is to learn whether it completes the same task with a better result, less operating burden, or both.

![Technician preparing matched stainless-steel coupons for a controlled cleaning trial](/img/blog/industrial-cleaning-trial.webp)

![Four-step controlled industrial cleaning trial](/img/blog/diagrams/trial-method.svg)

## Diagnose the actual job

Name the asset, substrate, soil or deposit, temperature, current chemistry, application method, and available window. Then define what clean enough means.

Scale and rust point toward mineral-removal chemistry. Grease, oil, protein, and organic film point toward wetting, sequestration, and soil lift. Mixed soils may need a sequence.

## Hold the comparison steady

Use equal areas or matched parts. Keep soil load, agitation, dwell, temperature, rinse method, and acceptance endpoint as consistent as field conditions allow.

| Control | Hold constant | Measure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Surface | Alloy, coating, age | Finish and material condition |
| Soil | Type and loading | Removal at the endpoint |
| Method | Dose, dwell, agitation | Passes, labor, and water |
| Release | Same acceptance rule | Downtime and rework |

## Isolate, contain, release

Start on a coupon, removable part, or bounded area. Protect drains and adjacent materials. Confirm the wastewater path before product touches the asset.

Release the area only after the surface, rinse, and operating endpoint pass the facility’s own criteria. A good result without a safe restart is not a completed task.

## Count the operating difference

Every offered VertKleen product is HMIS 0-0-0. That removes much of the hazard burden that follows conventional acid, caustic, and solvent workflows.

Still follow the current label, SDS, dilution, and site procedure. Record odor, handling, ventilation, PPE, isolation, rinse demand, cleanup, and crew feedback beside cleaning performance.

## Turn one win into a method

Capture product, lot, concentration, application, contact time, agitation, water, labor, before-and-after images, surface condition, and completed-task cost.

That record becomes the starting SOP, training aid, purchasing case, and baseline for the next asset. No folklore. No gallon-price guess.

## Build the trial with MASEST

MASEST can match the soil to the product, define the controlled trial, and return the result as a reusable operating brief.

[[card:title=See published VertKleen field results|href=/proof|image=/img/proof/cases/farm-rust-after.webp|alt=Metal after a documented VertKleen cleaning trial|width=740|height=967]]

## Trial references

Use the [product catalog](/products), [published field results](/proof), and [application methods and product files](/resources) to build the comparison.

Send the current chemical, task, asset, soil, and desired endpoint through the [trial-plan intake](/contact?type=audit).

blog_posts.title: Food-plant CIP: match each cleaning stage to the soil
blog_posts.body:
## One circuit can hold two different soils

Protein, fat, yeast, and organic film are not the same problem as beer stone, carbonate scale, and rust. Asking one cleaner to do both jobs often stretches time, dose, and rinse water.

Start by mapping the circuit, soil, metallurgy, flow, temperature, dead legs, drain points, and current release endpoint. The cycle should follow the soil, not habit.

![Five-stage soil-matched clean-in-place cycle](/img/blog/diagrams/cip-cycle.svg)

## Use CR for the organic load

VertKleen CIP CR uses alkalinity, wetting, and sequestration to loosen protein, fat, yeast, krausen, and organic film. Flow and agitation carry released soil toward the drain.

The useful endpoint is not elapsed time alone. Track visible load, return clarity, concentration, temperature, and the rinse condition required by the facility procedure.

## Use HCR for beer stone and scale

After the organic load and CR are rinsed out, VertKleen CIP HCR targets beer stone, carbonate scale, rust, and mineral film. It uses controlled mineral-removal chemistry instead of a blunt acid step.

Do not mix stages. Confirm chemical clearance before changing products, and match concentration and contact time to the deposit, circuit, and current product instructions.

## Keep cleaning and sanitation distinct

Cleaning removes soil that can shield microorganisms or consume sanitizer. It does not replace the facility’s validated sanitation, verification, or production-release program.

The final rinse, sanitizer, inspection, testing, and release decision remain controlled by the food-safety plan, equipment requirements, and site SOP.

## Measure return to production

A faster chemical reaction is useful only if the whole line returns sooner. Count preparation, circulation, rinsing, testing, corrective work, and release as completed-cycle cost.

| Cycle input | Record | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chemistry | Product, dose, temperature | Repeatability |
| Time | Setup through release | True downtime |
| Water | Pre-rinse and final rinse | Utility and wastewater load |
| Result | Soil, beer stone, rinse endpoint | Production readiness |

## Use the 0-0-0 operating advantage

Every VertKleen product MASEST currently offers is HMIS 0-0-0, including CIP CR and CIP HCR. That changes receiving, handling, isolation, and crew experience around a demanding cycle.

Current labels, SDS files, dilution, and site controls still govern use. Lower hazard does not remove the need for disciplined chemical separation and verified release.

## Start from field evidence

MASEST holds CR and HCR brewery records from seven Florida breweries, covering tanks, kegs, lines, heat exchangers, organic soil, and beer-stone work.

[[card:title=Review the brewery CIP field record|href=/proof#brewery-cip-trials|image=/img/proof/cases/brewery.webp|alt=Brewery equipment documented in VertKleen CIP trials|width=1200|height=900]]

## CIP references

Use the [CIP review intake](/contact?type=audit&industry=Food%20%26%20Beverage) to send the circuit, soil, current cycle, and desired release time.

blog_posts.title: Cooling-tower cleaning belongs inside the water-management plan
blog_posts.body:
## Cleaning is one event inside a living system

A cooling tower never stops changing. Makeup water, evaporation, heat, airborne debris, metallurgy, dose, and biology keep moving the operating target.

That is why periodic cleaning cannot stand alone. It should remove established load, restore inspectable surfaces, and return the tower to a controlled water-management program.

![Cooling-tower maintenance and cleaning program](/img/blog/diagrams/tower-program.svg)

## Give every chemistry one role

WaterSafe60 supports recurring scale and corrosion control. Purgo supports scoped organic-load and odor control. HCR or Descaler removes established mineral scale and corrosion deposits.

| Need | VertKleen role | Program moment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scale pressure | WaterSafe60 | Recurring treatment |
| Organic load and odor | Purgo | Monitored program dose |
| Established mineral deposit | HCR or Descaler | Planned cleaning window |
| Mixed oily soil | Task-matched soil lift | Isolated cleaning step |

## Inspect before selecting chemistry

Record tower duty, volume, metallurgy, fill condition, deposit location, current treatment, water data, circulation path, and shutdown window. Photograph representative surfaces.

A carbonate deposit needs mineral removal. Oily film needs soil lift. Organic residue needs a different control strategy. One product should not be asked to solve every tower problem.

## Build the shutdown backward from restart

Define isolation, circulation, access, containment, rinse volume, wastewater route, inspection, refill, dose restoration, and operating release before the cleaning begins.

That sequence protects the maintenance window. It also exposes where labor, water, contractor time, or unclear acceptance criteria are likely to delay restart.

## Use the 0-0-0 line where crews feel it

Every VertKleen product MASEST offers is HMIS 0-0-0. For tower teams, that can simplify freight, storage, work-area coordination, and technician experience.

The exact label, SDS, dilution, water-management plan, discharge rules, and site procedure still control the work. Product hazard is one input, not the whole program.

## Verify the endpoint

Record dose, crew time, rinse water, deposit change, fill condition, surface condition, and return-to-service time. Compare completed-system cost with the prior method.

Cleaning is complete when the defined surfaces and operating checks pass—not when the drum is empty or the planned hours expire.

## Keep the result inside the WMP

Add the cleaning record, images, findings, corrective actions, restart values, and next inspection trigger to the water-management file. That makes the event useful after the crew leaves.

[[card:title=See MASEST water-management and treatment services|href=/programs|image=/img/industries/samples/hvac-water.webp|alt=Representative cooling-tower and HVAC water-system maintenance|width=840|height=520]]

## Program references

Use the [water-treatment programs](/programs), [VertKleen products](/products), and [field results](/proof) to plan the maintenance window.

Use the [tower-program review](/contact?type=audit&industry=HVAC%20%2F%20Water%20Treatment) to send system volume, metallurgy, treatment, and deposit.

blog_posts.title: Beer line cleaner cost: compare the complete CIP cycle
blog_posts.body:
## Bottle price hides the real bill

A cleaner can look inexpensive and still create an expensive cycle. Dose, circulation, rinse water, labor, repeat passes, downtime, and release determine what the brewery actually pays.

Compare completed cycles on the same line and soil load. A fair result includes clean equipment, a verified rinse, and release back to production.

## Beer lines carry two soil families

Yeast, protein, fat, and organic film respond to alkaline soil lift. Beer stone, carbonate scale, and rust need controlled mineral removal. One chemistry rarely does both jobs efficiently.

| Soil or deposit | VertKleen stage | Job to complete |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Yeast and protein | CIP CR | Wet, lift, and carry organic soil |
| Fat and organic film | CIP CR | Break loading and limit redeposition |
| Beer stone and carbonate | CIP HCR | Release mineral deposit |
| Rust and mineral film | CIP HCR | Remove deposit before final rinse |

## Sequence CR, rinse, then HCR

CIP CR uses alkalinity, wetting, and sequestration for the organic load. After a verified rinse, CIP HCR follows with controlled mineral-removal chemistry for beer stone and scale.

Do not mix stages. Record dose, temperature, circulation, rinse endpoint, and the facility’s sanitation and release steps for each circuit.

## Compare the incumbent fairly

Micro Matic describes its alkaline beer-line cleaner as caustic and recommends a 2–3% use concentration. Its own cleaning program also separates alkaline and acid work.

That makes cycle design—not sticker price—the useful comparison. Test equal circuits and include every stage required to reach the same endpoint.

[[card:title=Review Micro Matic’s current beer-line cleaning guidance|href=https://www.micromatic.com/en-us/seo/cleaningequip-top/cleaningchemicals-top/beer-line-cleaning-chemicals-bot|image=/img/proof/cases/brewery.webp|alt=Brewery piping and tank used for clean-in-place work|width=1200|height=900]]

## Put HMIS 0-0-0 into the economics

Every offered VertKleen product is HMIS 0-0-0, including CIP CR and CIP HCR. That can reduce the handling, storage, work-area, and crew burden surrounding a recurring chemical cycle.

The current label, SDS, dilution, food-area procedure, sanitation step, and production-release check still govern use.

## Price one completed cycle

CR lists at [[price:VK-CR-2.5G|hvac|per_gallon]] and HCR at [[price:VK-HCR-2.5G|hvac|per_gallon]] in the CIP pricing set. Apply actual use rates instead of comparing undiluted gallons.

| Cost input | What to record |
| --- | --- |
| Chemistry | Product, concentration, and gallons used |
| Utilities | Water, heat, and pump time |
| Labor | Setup, circulation, rinse, and verification |
| Production | Total line downtime |
| Quality | Rework, failed rinse, or repeat cycle |

## Start with the brewery field record

MASEST holds CR and HCR records from seven Florida breweries, covering tanks, kegs, lines, heat exchangers, organic soil, and beer-stone work.

blog_posts.title: CR HD vs Simple Green for heavy industrial degreasing
blog_posts.body:
## Start with the soil load

Simple Green Industrial is a broad cleaner and degreaser with use guidance from full strength to 1:10 for many jobs. That range can suit routine facility cleaning.

Heavy petroleum grease, tracked oil, carbon, and old shop soil create a different test. On floors, forklifts, drains, and parts, the question is how many passes reach the endpoint.

## CR HD is built for the heavier job

VertKleen CR HD combines high-pH wetting, sequestration, and surfactant lift. Wetting enters the film, surfactants lift soil, and sequestration controls hard-water ions and redeposition.

The aim is not maximum foam. It is controlled contact, soil release, rinse-out, and fewer repeat passes at the right dilution.

## Compare the products without caricature

Simple Green says its Industrial Cleaner & Degreaser is EPA Safer Choice recognized and needs no special PPE for intended use. A fair comparison should respect that profile.

CR HD’s case is stronger soil capacity plus an HMIS 0-0-0 profile. Prove the difference on the same surface, soil loading, dilution, dwell, agitation, rinse, and endpoint.

| Decision factor | CR HD | Simple Green Industrial |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary fit | Heavy hydrocarbon and industrial soil | Broad cleaning and degreasing |
| Use strategy | Task-matched dilution and contact | Full strength to 1:10 by job |
| VertKleen claim | HMIS 0-0-0 | Use current Simple Green SDS |
| Best metric | Passes and completed-task cost | Passes and completed-task cost |

[[card:title=Review Simple Green’s current product guidance|href=https://simplegreen.com/industrial/products/industrial-cleaner-degreaser/|image=/img/products/crhd-studio.webp|alt=Heavy-duty industrial degreasing product and application equipment|width=900|height=1200]]

## Use the 0-0-0 advantage accurately

Every offered VertKleen product is HMIS 0-0-0. For CR HD, that pairs heavy-duty soil lift with a lower-hazard operating profile.

That does not erase procedure. Keep the current label and SDS with the method, protect the surface, control runoff, and verify the rinse and release endpoint.

## Count the completed task

CR HD lists at [[price:VK-CRHD-5G|retail|per_gallon]]. Compare actual use cost; competitor shelf prices change and say little about soil capacity.

| Cost input | Measure on both sides |
| --- | --- |
| Product | Diluted gallons used |
| Work | Dwell, agitation, and passes |
| Utilities | Rinse water and equipment time |
| Operations | Area closure and downtime |

blog_posts.title: Industrial descaling without the conventional mineral-acid burden
blog_posts.body:
## Scale charges rent every operating hour

Carbonate scale narrows flow and insulates heat-transfer surfaces. The system pays through longer run time, higher energy demand, unstable temperatures, restricted capacity, and unplanned shutdown risk.

A descaling job must recover performance without trading the deposit for uncontrolled material attack, fumes, or a difficult restart.

## This is controlled chemistry, not magic

VertKleen HCR and Descaler use controlled hydrogen-ion activity to consume carbonate scale: `2 H+ + CaCO3 → Ca2+ + CO2 + H2O`.

Complexing, wetting, and inhibition help released material move toward rinse-out. The products are not “acid-free”; they replace a conventional mineral-acid workflow with controlled mineral removal.

## The evidence changes the risk calculation

Source testing reports a 0.59 mpy steel-corrosion rate for HCR—up to 280× less corrosion than hydrochloric acid under the reported comparison.

The same source record reports 15% more calcium-carbonate capacity than hydrochloric acid. That combination targets scale while protecting more of the equipment value around it.

## Plan the full circulation loop

![Closed-loop industrial descaling plan](/img/blog/diagrams/descaling-loop.svg)

| Stage | Control | Release evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scope | Volume, metallurgy, deposit | Trial plan and compatibility review |
| Circulate | Dose, flow, temperature, gas | Deposit response and stable operation |
| Rinse | Water, pH, solids path | Defined rinse endpoint |
| Restart | Inspection and system checks | Flow, temperature, and surface condition |

Record circulation time, crew time, water, wastewater, surface condition, and complete shutdown duration. A fast reaction is not a win if the system waits on rinse or repair.

## Choose HCR or Descaler by the job

HCR fits industrial scale and rust work where circulation, equipment value, and deposit capacity matter. Descaler gives facilities a dedicated mineral-scale option for matched systems and procedures.

MASEST can confirm product, dose, material fit, and trial boundary from the asset, deposit, metallurgy, volume, and current method.

## Put HMIS 0-0-0 beside performance

Every offered VertKleen product is HMIS 0-0-0, including HCR and Descaler. That can simplify freight, receiving, storage, crew coordination, and the work area around a planned outage.

Follow the current label, SDS, dilution, gas-management, wastewater, and site procedure. Lower hazard supports disciplined work; it does not replace it.

## A field result worth testing against

At DDC, the recorded incumbent CLR trial ran 36 hours without clearing the deposit. HCR then cleared 20 years of rust and scale in 30 minutes.

That field record is not a universal cycle promise. It is a strong reason to run a controlled HCR trial on the actual system and count the completed job.

Request a [scale review](/contact?type=quote) with the deposit, metallurgy, system volume, and current cycle.

VertKleen HCR targets the same industrial decision with controlled hydrogen-ion activity, wetting, complexing, and inhibition—plus an HMIS 0-0-0 profile.

## Compare published strengths, then test the asset

| Decision factor | VertKleen HCR | RYDLYME |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary use | Carbonate scale and rust | Water-scale deposits |

The published numbers use different reference methods. Do not treat them as a direct laboratory head-to-head. Use them to design a matched field trial.

## HMIS 0-0-0 is part of the cycle

Keep the current label and SDS in the trial file. Follow site controls for isolation, circulation, ventilation, rinse, wastewater, inspection, and restart.

blog_posts.title: HMIS 0-0-0: what it means—and what it changes
blog_posts.body:
## Every offered VertKleen product is 0-0-0

MASEST now offers 15 VertKleen products, and every one is HMIS 0-0-0. The former non-0-0-0 product is no longer offered.

That gives the current line one clear operating story: cleaning performance without the hazard profile that often surrounds industrial acid, caustic, bleach, and solvent work.

![HMIS 0-0-0 explained for the current VertKleen line](/img/blog/diagrams/hmis-000.svg)

## Read the three digits in order

HMIS uses three numeric fields from 0 to 4. A zero is the lowest rating in its field. The rating belongs to the exact product and current documentation.

| Position | HMIS field | VertKleen rating |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First | Health | 0 |
| Second | Flammability | 0 |
| Third | Physical hazard | 0 |

## Zero does not mean “ignore the label”

HMIS 0-0-0 does not turn an industrial product into drinking water. It does not replace the label, SDS, dilution, surface check, wastewater plan, or site SOP.

Standard work hygiene still applies. Avoid unnecessary contact, use the product for its intended task, and follow current first-aid and handling instructions.

## The rating changes more than PPE

A chemical’s operating burden begins before application and continues after cleaning. Freight, receiving, storage, training, area coordination, spill planning, rinse, cleanup, and release all consume time.

VertKleen’s 0-0-0 profile can simplify those steps while keeping the cleaning result at the center of the decision.

| Workflow point | Question to compare |
| --- | --- |
| Freight | Hazmat classification or surcharge? |
| Receiving | Special segregation or paperwork? |
| Setup | Ventilation, clearance, or isolation burden? |
| Use | Crew controls and handling experience? |
| Finish | Rinse, cleanup, wastewater, and release? |

## One line is easier to standardize

A universal 0-0-0 profile reduces exceptions across a multi-product program. Teams can match chemistry to soil without reintroducing a high-hazard outlier from the same offered line.

That helps purchasing, safety, maintenance, and operations discuss the same portfolio with a consistent baseline. The task method stays product-specific.

## It supports global movement

VertKleen works across 50+ countries. The 0-0-0 profile supports a cleaner receiving and handling story for distributors, facilities, contractors, and international programs.

Local transport, import, workplace, and discharge rules still apply. Confirm the current documents and destination requirements for each shipment.

## Put handling beside performance

Do not choose a cleaner on HMIS alone. Compare deposit or soil removal, material condition, dose, passes, water, labor, downtime, wastewater, and completed-task cost.

Then place the 0-0-0 operating profile beside those results. That is where lower hazard becomes a measurable business advantage instead of a label footnote.

blog_posts.title: VertKleen LAM3 vs Wet & Forget: compare the finished area
blog_posts.body:
## Exterior cleaning is a time-and-area problem

Moss, algae, mildew, lichen, and visible staining do not leave every surface on the same clock. Shade, moisture, porosity, weather, and growth depth change the result.

That makes bottle price a weak comparison. Measure treated area, labor, visible change, adjacent-material condition, and maintenance interval.

## How Wet & Forget is designed to work

Wet & Forget directs users to dilute its concentrate 1:5, saturate a dry surface, and let weathering remove stains over time. Its site says results may take days to months.

The company positions it as a no-scrub, no-rinse treatment with annual use or reapplication as needed. Those are useful strengths when a gradual result fits the property.

[[card:title=Review Wet & Forget’s current use directions|href=https://www.wetandforget.com/wet-and-forget-concentrate.html|image=/img/proof/cases/grout-moss.webp|alt=Exterior masonry with moss and organic staining|width=919|height=690]]

## How LAM3 approaches the same outcome

VertKleen LAM3 extends wetting and dwell across exterior organic growth and visible staining. Purgo support continues working on the organic matrix after application.

The practical question is how that program changes the finished area, labor, runoff, return visit, and maintenance interval on the actual substrate.

## Compare equal test areas

Choose matched areas with the same substrate, stain, shade, weather, slope, and drainage. Mark camera positions and photograph the baseline.

Record mixed volume, coverage, wet dwell, runoff handling, visible change, adjacent materials, labor, and inspection dates. Judge both areas on the same day and endpoint.

| Trial input | Hold constant | Measure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Surface | Material, age, and coating | Finish and material condition |
| Growth | Type, depth, and shade | Visible change over time |
| Weather | Dry window and exposure | Time to endpoint |
| Method | Area and application tool | Product, labor, and runoff |

## Use field evidence, not instant-result theater

MASEST records LAM3/Purgo work on a painted exterior column with visible improvement after two weeks. That supports a long-dwell program, not an artificial same-minute reveal.

A fair trial should photograph the same area over the interval promised by each method. It should also record any brushing, rinsing, or repeat application.

## Add the HMIS 0-0-0 difference

Every offered VertKleen product is HMIS 0-0-0, including LAM3 and Purgo. That can simplify storage, technician handling, and property coordination around recurring exterior work.

Follow the current label, SDS, dilution, runoff plan, landscape protections, and substrate guidance. Test a small area before broad application.

## Price by finished area

LAM3 lists at [[price:VK-LAM3-5G|retail|per_gallon]]. Wet & Forget pricing changes by retailer and package, so use the current delivered price in the trial.

| Cost input | Calculation |

| Access | Lift, hose, protection, and travel |

blog_posts.title: VertKleen HCR vs CLR PRO MAX for industrial descaling
blog_posts.body:
## CLR PRO MAX is an industrial product

A useful comparison starts with the current product, not an outdated caricature. CLR PRO MAX is sold for heavy industrial descaling, rust, lime, and calcium work.

Its technical data starts heavy-duty applications at 1:1 and lists a 2–3 hour use window. Its current SDS classifies the sold product and use dilution for serious skin and eye hazards.

[[card:title=Review the current CLR PRO MAX product information|href=https://www.clrbrands.com/proline/products/clr-pro/clr-pro-max-industrial-descaler/|image=/img/proof/cases/farm-rust-after.webp|alt=Industrial metal after documented rust-and-scale removal|width=740|height=967]]

## HCR makes a different operating case

VertKleen HCR uses controlled hydrogen-ion activity to consume carbonate scale. Wetting, complexing, and inhibition support deposit release and rinse-out.

Every offered VertKleen product is HMIS 0-0-0. HCR pairs industrial scale and rust removal with that lower-hazard operating profile.

## Compare the published profiles

| Decision factor | VertKleen HCR | CLR PRO MAX |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary fit | Industrial carbonate scale and rust | Heavy industrial scale, rust, lime, calcium |
| Use plan | Task-matched trial | 1:1 starting dilution for heavy duty |
| Time | Set by deposit and system | TDS lists 2–3 hours |
| Hazard | HMIS 0-0-0 | Current SDS lists corrosive hazards |
| Economics | Completed-system cost | Completed-system cost |

Product claims and hazard systems are not a substitute for a matched trial. Compare the exact current products, documents, dose, metallurgy, and endpoint.

## HCR protects more of the asset value

Source testing reports HCR at 0.59 mpy on steel—up to 280× less corrosion than hydrochloric acid under the reported comparison.

The source record also reports 15% more calcium-carbonate capacity than hydrochloric acid. Those figures support an equipment-conscious trial on real deposit.

## Read the DDC result carefully

MASEST records an incumbent CLR trial at DDC running 36 hours without clearing the deposit. HCR then cleared 20 years of rust and scale in 30 minutes.

That trial may predate the current CLR PRO MAX formula, so it is not presented as a direct test of today’s product. It is field evidence for HCR’s capacity on a severe deposit.

## Price the verified restart

HCR lists at [[price:VK-HCR-5G|retail|per_gallon]]. Current CLR pricing varies, so enter the delivered price and actual use rate instead of freezing a shelf price.

| Cost input | Record |
| --- | --- |
| Chemistry | Concentration and gallons used |
| Labor | Setup, circulation, monitoring, and rinse |
| Water | Flush and final endpoint |
| Downtime | Isolation through verified restart |
| Asset | Deposit release and material condition |

## Run the comparison on the real system

Confirm volume, metallurgy, seals, coatings, deposit, temperature, circulation, gas release, wastewater, rinse, inspection, and restart criteria.

Request an [HCR trial](/contact?type=quote&product=VertKleen%20HCR%20vs%20CLR) with deposit, equipment volume, current concentration, and cycle.

blog_posts.body:
## Start with the cleaning problem

VertKleen is a 15-product system, not one universal jug. The fastest path to a good trial is to name the soil, surface, process, and endpoint before choosing chemistry.

Every product MASEST offers is HMIS 0-0-0. That gives the whole line one lower-hazard baseline while each formula keeps a specific job.

## Use this product selector

| Cleaning problem | Start with | Primary role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Carbonate scale and rust | HCR, HVAC HCR, Descaler | Controlled mineral removal |
| Organic and process soil | CR, HVAC CR | Wetting, lift, sequestration |
| Heavy grease and oil | CR HD, CR HD Low Foam | High soil-capacity degreasing |
| General facility soil | Neutral, MultiWash | Surface-matched maintenance cleaning |
| Organic load and odor | Purgo | Bio-active program support |
| Exterior growth and staining | LAM3 | Long-dwell exterior treatment |
| Aluminum oxide and brightening | AlumiBrite | Aluminum-focused cleaning |
| Wash and finish care | Torque | Vehicle and equipment wash |
| Specialty rust and scale | SAR | Matched mineral-deposit work |
| Recurring water treatment | WaterSafe60 | Scale and corrosion control |

## HCR, HVAC HCR, and Descaler

Use the mineral-removal group for carbonate scale, rust, and deposits in equipment, piping, HVAC, and water systems. Match the product to metallurgy, volume, deposit, circulation, and shutdown plan.

Source testing reports HCR at 0.59 mpy on steel, up to 280× less corrosion than hydrochloric acid, with 15% more calcium-carbonate capacity than HCl.

## CR, HVAC CR, and the CR HD family

CR and HVAC CR target organic soil through wetting, alkalinity, and sequestration. CR HD adds capacity for heavy hydrocarbon loading. Low Foam fits processes where foam control matters.

Use soil loading, dilution, passes, water, labor, and surface condition to choose among them. The strongest concentrate is not automatically the best process.

## Neutral and MultiWash

Neutral supports surface-conscious general cleaning. MultiWash covers mixed facility work where one practical maintenance cleaner can reduce product switching.

Confirm the substrate, soil, finish, application method, rinse, and release endpoint before standardizing either product.

## Purgo and LAM3

Purgo supports organic-load and odor programs. LAM3 extends wetting and dwell across moss, algae, mildew, lichen, and visible exterior staining.

Their value appears over the planned treatment interval. Record coverage, weather, visible change, labor, runoff, adjacent materials, and time to endpoint.

## AlumiBrite, Torque, SAR, and WaterSafe60

AlumiBrite targets aluminum cleaning and brightening. Torque supports wash-and-finish care. SAR handles matched rust-and-scale work. WaterSafe60 supports recurring scale and corrosion control.

These are specialist tools. Use the current product page, label, SDS, and a bounded trial to confirm the fit.

## One safety profile, 50+ countries

Every offered VertKleen product is HMIS 0-0-0, and the platform works across 50+ countries. That combination supports simpler portfolio, freight, receiving, storage, and training conversations.

Local rules and product-specific methods still apply. Keep the exact label, SDS, dilution, wastewater path, and site procedure connected to the task.

## Turn the match into a controlled trial

Name the asset, substrate, soil, current chemical, temperature, method, operating window, and acceptance endpoint. Isolate a coupon, part, or bounded area when possible.

Record concentration, contact time, agitation, passes, rinse water, crew time, wastewater, surface condition, downtime, and completed-task cost.

Use the [product catalog](/products), [decision guides](/resources#comparisons), and [field results](/proof) to prepare the switch.

[Request a product match](/contact?type=audit) with the soil, surface, current chemical, temperature, and desired result.
